info.title: blerg-runner
info.summary: Starts and drives coding-agent sessions on a Blerg install.
info.description: The public, agent-facing contract of blerg-runner (contract version v1). Paths are relative to this component's base URL, which GET /agents reports as base_url. The browser and daemon surfaces (WebSockets, board and ticket REST) are deliberately not described here: they are the product's own UI transport, not an API for agents.

tags.name: discovery
tags.description: Finding out what this component is and how to talk to it.

tags.name: sessions
tags.description: The session contract: start, drive, follow, collect.

tags.name: files
tags.description: A session's files: what the agent published and what a person attached.

get.summary: This component's agent manifest: auth and every operation.
get.description: No authentication. With `Accept: text/markdown` (or `?format=md`) the same document is returned as Markdown.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `md` returns the Markdown rendering instead of JSON.

get.summary: What the calling credential is: kind, subject, audience, capabilities, expiry.
get.description: Introspection of the bearer credential you just used. The static runner key has no subject or expiry and returns only `{"kind": "runner_key"}`. The credential itself is never echoed back.

get.summary: The models a session on an engine can run on, with each model's effort levels.
get.description: One list per engine (`claude`, `codex`, `hermes`, …). An engine with no model source answers 200 with an empty `models` list and `source: "none"` — there is nothing to pick, and `model`/`effort` stay unset. For `claude` the list is what Claude Code's own /model picker offers, taken from the public Claude Code model catalog (re-fetched every 6 hours; `source: "builtin"` means the compiled-in copy is being served because no fetch has succeeded or fetching is disabled). For `codex` and `hermes` the list is what a connected workstation daemon probed (`source: "daemon"`): `codex debug models` for Codex, and for Hermes the `/models` of the OpenAI-compatible endpoint its config names (only for `provider: custom`), re-probed every ~15 minutes. Pass `daemon_id` for that daemon's own list; without it, the one daemon that reported a list, or the union of all of them (lowest daemon id first). No report answers `source: "none"`. Models in section `main` come first, then `overflow`. Pass a model's `id` as `model` and one of its `efforts` as `effort` to POST /api/runner/start with the same `engine`. A model with an empty `efforts` list takes no effort. Also readable with a signed-in browser session token.

parameters.name: engine
parameters.description: Engine id, as POST /api/runner/start takes it (`claude` for the default engine).

parameters.name: daemon_id
parameters.description: The daemon the session will run on, for engines whose list a daemon reports (`codex`, `hermes`): that daemon's list, or `source: "none"` when it reported none — never another daemon's. Ignored by `claude`.

post.summary: Start a coding-agent session on a repository.
post.description: Runs the session in a cluster Job when a cluster runtime is configured, otherwise on a connected workstation daemon: in its local sandbox container when the daemon has the sandbox image, else on its host. Pass `runtime` to choose explicitly. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make a retry safe: the same key with the same body replays the original `202` with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same key with a different body is a `409`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1-128 characters, scoped to the calling credential, retained 24 h.

202.description: The session was accepted; follow it with the events or result operations.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: Present and `true` when this response replays an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key.

get.summary: Session status: lifecycle, runtime, whether it can be resumed.
get.description: Status is deliberately not one string: `lifecycle` is the session state machine, `runtime` describes the hosting layer, `resumable` says whether a dead session can be revived by the next message.

post.summary: Send a conversational turn to the session; resumes a disconnected one.

text.description: The turn to deliver. Required and non-empty.

source.description: Who is speaking, for the transcript. Defaults to `runner`.

409.description: The session has ended and takes no messages.

post.summary: Cancel the session's in-flight turn without ending it.

409.description: The session has no live runtime to interrupt.

post.summary: End the session for good and free its runtime slot.
post.description: Idempotent: stopping an already-stopped session is still `200`. Finished work must call this or cluster session slots leak.

get.summary: Read a window of the session transcript from a cursor.
get.description: Poll with `after_seq` set to the highest `seq` you have seen. `has_more` is true when the window was truncated by `limit`. With `before_seq` the window is instead the `limit` events just before that sequence number (0 = the end of the transcript), oldest first, and the reply adds `has_older`, `first_seq` and `server_time` — the page a chat loads above what the live stream opened with.

parameters.name: after_seq
parameters.description: Return only events with a higher sequence number. Default 0 (from the start).

parameters.name: before_seq
parameters.description: Page backwards: the `limit` events with a lower sequence number, oldest first; 0 means from the end. Takes precedence over `after_seq`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum events to return. Default 200, maximum 400.

get.summary: The same events as a Server-Sent Events stream.
get.description: Each event carries `id: <seq>`, `event: <kind>` and the payload JSON as `data`. Resume after a disconnect with `Last-Event-ID` (or `?after_seq=`). A `: keepalive` comment is sent every 15 s; a final `event: end` carries the result payload when the session is terminal, then the stream closes.

parameters.name: after_seq
parameters.description: Start after this sequence number; `Last-Event-ID` takes precedence.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The last `id` you received, for transparent resumption.

get.summary: The live transcript as Server-Sent Events: a replay page, then every event, typing delta and status change as it happens.
get.description: What the runner's own browser gets over its websocket, for the credential that started the session — straight from the hub, not a database poll. Frames are `event: <type>` + `data: <json>`, with `id: <seq>` on persisted events only. `agent_event`: an AgentEvent (`type, session_id, client_event_id, seq, ts, kind, payload`; `transient: true` on a typing delta, which has no seq and is never persisted — the same `client_event_id` may arrive twice across the replay and the live feed, so deduplicate on it). `replay_done`: once after the opening page (`session_id, last_seq, has_more, server_time`; with `tail=1` also `older: true, has_older, first_seq`). `status`: `{session_id, status}` (`starting, running, waiting, idle, disconnected, stopped, ended, error`), plus `message`, `end_reason`, `ended_by` when known — once at open, then on every change. `end`: the Result body when the session is over; the stream then closes. A `: keepalive` comment is sent every 15 s of silence. The hub carries a session's deltas only while its host is connected to this runner; for the durable record alone use events/stream.

parameters.name: after_seq
parameters.description: Replay forward from this sequence number (exclusive). Default 0: from the start. Ignored with `tail=1`.

parameters.name: tail
parameters.description: `1` replays the newest `limit` events instead, marking the page `older` so a client pages backwards with `GET …/events?before_seq=<first_seq>`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Size of the opening page. Default 200, maximum 400.

get.summary: The session's files (published by the agent or attached by a person), newest first, with versions.
get.description: The same list the runner's browser shows in its Files panel. A file published again under the same name and origin is the next `version` of it; `latest_version` is the highest version of that name.

get.summary: One file's bytes for an in-app viewer, with the server-chosen content type.
get.description: Hardened exactly as the browser route is: the stored (server-classified) content type for images, PDFs and the text types that are safe to render, `application/octet-stream` for anything else; always `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`, `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

get.summary: One file's bytes as an attachment.
get.description: `Content-Disposition: attachment` with the file's name — the plain name for the newest version of it, `<stem>-v<N><ext>` for an older one. Same hardening headers as the raw route.

delete.summary: Delete one of the session's files, whichever origin it came from.
delete.description: A file is deleted by whoever may see the session. Idempotent in effect: a file that is already gone is a 404.

post.summary: Attach a person's file to the session (raw body, X-Artifact-Name header), for the agent to fetch.
post.description: The body is the file; the name comes from `X-Artifact-Name` (percent-encoded) or `?name=`, sanitised to a base name. The content type is classified by the server from the name and bytes — the request's `Content-Type` is never used. Stored with `origin: user`, attributed to the account the credential acts for (the app vouches for the person). Caps, as on the browser route: 25 MiB per file, 20 attachments and 200 MiB per session, 20 versions per name; an ended session takes no more.

parameters.name: X-Artifact-Name
parameters.description: The file's name, percent-encoded. `?name=` is the alternative.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The file's name when the header is not sent.

409.description: The session has ended, or a cap is reached (files, bytes, or versions of this name).

413.description: The file is larger than 25 MiB.

get.summary: The UI packages this runner distributes.
get.description: No authentication. `{packages: [{name, version, file, sha512, url}]}` — the same package GET /agents advertises as `ui.chat_package`. 404 when this build packed none.

404.description: No package is packed into this build.

get.summary: A package tarball, by the name the package list gives it.
get.description: No authentication. `npm i <this url>` installs it. Served with `Content-Type: application/gzip` and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` — the name carries the version, so a new version is a new URL. Only names the package list contains are served; anything else is 404.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The `file` of a package list entry, e.g. `blerglab-chat-0.1.0.tgz`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The package name within the scope, e.g. `chat`.

get.summary: The structured outcome: terminal state, branch, last assistant message.

200.description: The session's result so far; `terminal` says whether it is final.

SessionId.name: id
SessionId.description: The session id returned by the start operation.

ArtifactId.name: aid
ArtifactId.description: A file id from the session's file list (or an `artifact` event's payload).

agentToken.description: A core-signed agent token minted from the `run-sessions` preset (`aud: "blerg-runner"`, capability `session.start`). Get one from core: POST /api/tokens, or Settings → Agent tokens.

runnerKey.description: The operator's static runner key (BLERG_RUNNER_KEY). A component credential with no owning account; sessions it starts run on the operator's credentials. When it is unset the whole session contract answers 404.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, expired, revoked or under-capable bearer credential.

NotConfigured.description: The runner contract is not enabled on this install (no runner key configured).

NotFound.description: No such session — or one this credential may not see: an agent token is scoped to the sessions its owner started, and a session outside that scope is reported exactly as an unknown one.

Unprocessable.description: The request was understood but rejected: unknown or unsafe repo name, a reserved env key, an unusable callback_url, a runtime that is not `cluster`, `docker` or `daemon`, a `model` that is not a well-formed model name, an `effort` outside the engine's allowlist, or `runtime: cluster` on an install with no cluster configured.

IdempotencyConflict.description: The Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request body.

ServerError.description: The session could not be recorded (database or idempotency store unavailable). The request was not started; retry.

NoRuntime.description: No runtime can take the session: no cluster capacity, no connected daemon has the repo, or an idempotency record raced — retry.

DaemonBusy.description: The session's host is not connected (a desktop daemon restarting; Retry-After is set) or is not accepting messages right now. The message was not delivered; retry.

source.description: `live`: the engine's own list, last fetched successfully. `builtin`: the list compiled into this build. `daemon`: probed on a connected workstation daemon from the engine's own CLI or endpoint (Codex, Hermes). `none`: no source for this engine, or no daemon reported a list for it; `models` is empty.

fetched_at.description: When the live or daemon list was fetched (for a union of several daemons' lists, the oldest of them); null otherwise.

daemon_id.description: For `source: "daemon"`: the daemon whose list this is. Absent for a union of several daemons' lists, and for every other source.

engine_efforts.description: The engine's whole effort allowlist, lowest first (empty when it takes no effort) — the levels a model that is not in `models` (typed by hand) may be run at.

id.description: The model id to pass as `model`, e.g. `claude-sonnet-5`.

section.description: `main` models are the picker's headline choices; `overflow` are older or alternate versions.

efforts.description: Effort levels this model accepts, lowest first — a subset of the engine's allowlist (Claude: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`; Codex: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, `ultra`; Hermes: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, `ultra`). Empty when the model takes no effort.

default_effort.description: The model's default effort. Absent when `efforts` is empty, and also when the engine does not say (Hermes): then sending no `effort` leaves it to the engine's own configuration.

effort_kind.description: Optional: what the effort control means for this engine (e.g. `reasoning`), for display.

kind.description: `runner_key` is the static operator key; the others come from a core-signed token.

sub.description: The token id. Absent for the runner key.

on_behalf_of.description: The account the token acts for; attribution, never authorization.

aud.description: The audience the token was minted for: always `blerg-runner` here.

expires_at.description: Unix seconds. Absent for the runner key.

StartRequest.description: `repo` is required unless `no_repo` is true, in which case `repo`, `git_url` and `provider` must be absent (422 otherwise). A blank `repo` without `no_repo` is refused with 422 `repo is required`, as it always was.

repo.description: A folder name or `org/name` (one slash at most, no `..`, no leading dot). On a daemon runtime it must exist under the daemon's repos root. Required unless `no_repo` is true.

no_repo.description: Start a session tied to no repository. Must be set explicitly — a blank `repo` alone is never read as this. On the cluster the pod works in an empty directory that goes away with it: nothing is cloned and no git credential is given to it. On a daemon (`docker` or `daemon`) the session runs in a new, empty scratch folder under the daemon's repos root, named `.scratch-` plus a generated suffix; being dot-prefixed, it never appears in the daemon's folder list. The folder stays on that disk after the session ends. Any connected daemon may be chosen. The session's `repo` reads back as `""` (cluster) or that scratch folder name (daemon).

git_url.description: Clone URL override for cross-org repositories or another git provider, e.g. `https://gitlab.com/group/project.git` (cluster runtime only). A git token is only ever sent to the host it belongs to: the launcher's personal token for a registered provider's host (GitHub: github.com, GitLab: gitlab.com), or the install's shared token for its own configured git base. A URL on any other host is cloned with no token at all, so only a public repository clones there.

provider.description: The git provider `repo` lives on. Honoured on every runtime: a cluster clone comes from that provider's host with the caller's token for it, and a daemon never resolves the repo on another provider. Absent means GitHub, as before this field existed — pass it for any repository not on GitHub, or an `owner/name` is cloned from github.com. With `git_url`, the URL must be on this provider's host (422 otherwise).

title.description: A human-readable label for the session.

model.description: Engine-specific model name; the install's default when empty. An `id` from GET /api/models/{engine}; for Claude also a Claude Code alias such as `sonnet` or `sonnet[1m]` (lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `-`, `[`, `]`, at most 64 characters). Other engines: letters, digits and `. _ : / @ - [ ]`, not starting with `-`, at most 128 characters.

effort.description: Reasoning effort (see the model's `efforts` in GET /api/models/{engine}); the model's own default when empty. Must be in the engine's allowlist — Claude: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`; Codex: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, `ultra`; Hermes: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, `ultra`; an engine with no effort levels (today: OpenClaw) refuses any non-empty value with 422 — and, for a model the engine's list knows, in that model's own `efforts`. A daemon-reported list (Codex, Hermes) is per workstation and this call does not name one, so for those engines only the allowlist is checked here.

env.description: Extra environment for the session. Keys beginning `BLERG_RUNNER_`, and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, are reserved and rejected.

callback_url.description: Webhook for session completion. https, or http to localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1] and only where the install sets BLERG_RUNNER_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true (the desktop stack does; a cluster install rejects such a URL with 422). Redirects are not followed.

callback_secret.description: HMAC-SHA256 key for the webhook's X-Blerg-Signature header. Never returned by any endpoint.

engine.description: Coding engine to run. Defaults to `claude`.

runtime.description: Where to run it: a cluster Job (`cluster`), the local sandbox container on a connected daemon (`docker`), or that daemon's bare host (`daemon`). Defaults to `cluster` when a cluster runtime is configured, else `docker` when the chosen daemon has the sandbox image, else `daemon`. The sandbox reaches the board and the runner over the `blerg-sandbox` network but holds no git credentials, so its agent can commit but not push; pass `daemon` to run on the host instead. An explicit `docker` is honoured even where the image is missing — the daemon reports that.

auto_stop.description: One-shot: the runner stops the session itself once the first turn after the prompt is done — same effect as POST /stop, so `result.terminal` becomes true and the completion webhook fires without the caller stopping anything. Defaults to false: the session stays up waiting for more messages.

interaction.description: Whether a person is reading the session's chat as it works. `unattended` (the default on this contract): nobody is, so the agent is told not to stop and wait for an answer in the chat, to make the reasonable decision, note its assumption and end with a summary that stands on its own. `interactive`: a person is reading and answers in the chat, so the agent is told to talk a remark through before changing anything, to ask and end its turn when the decision is theirs, and to say what it is doing as it works. Pass `interactive` when the session is a conversation a person will follow as it happens. Any other value is a 400. A session a cron starts is always `unattended`. The mode is fixed at start and reported back as `interaction` by GET /api/runner/sessions/{id}.

runtime.description: The hosting layer, not the session state — and not the session's `runtime` field: a session hosted by a daemon reads `daemon` here whether its engine runs on that host or in its local sandbox. `GET /api/sessions` carries that distinction.

resumable.description: Whether the next message can revive a dead session.

auto_stop.description: Whether this session was started one-shot: the runner ends it when its first turn is done.

interaction.description: The session's interaction mode, as decided at start: `interactive` (a person is reading its chat as it works, and the agent was told so) or `unattended` (nobody is). Never empty: a session started before the mode was recorded reads `interactive` when a person started it in the app and `unattended` when a tool, a cron or the runner key did.

error_reason.description: Why it failed; empty unless the lifecycle is `error`.

EndReason.description: Why the session ended, from a fixed vocabulary; empty while it has not ended, and for sessions that ended before the runner recorded reasons. `stopped_by_user` / `stopped_by_agent`: a stop was requested (by a person, or by an agent token, service or the runner key). `auto_stopped`: the one-shot `auto_stop` ended it after its first turn. `process_exited` / `process_failed`: the process exited on its own, cleanly or not. `start_failed`: it never got going. `job_*`, `not_resumed`, `daemon_lost`, `daemon_unreported`: the runner's reconciler closed it out (the Job finished, failed or vanished; a disconnected session was not resumed within a day; its daemon did not come back; its daemon no longer had it). The first reason recorded wins: a stop is not overwritten by the process exit it causes. For failures `error_reason` still carries the detail. Treat a value you do not know as "ended"; the set may grow.

EndedBy.description: What kind of actor ended the session; null when none did (a process exit, a failed Job, the reconciler). Never identifies the account.

has_more.description: Forward paging only: the window was truncated by `limit`. Always false for a `before_seq` page.

has_older.description: `before_seq` pages only: events older than this page remain.

first_seq.description: `before_seq` pages only: the oldest seq in this page (0 when empty) — the next page's `before_seq`.

server_time.description: `before_seq` pages only: the server's clock when the page was read.

id.description: The file id (`aid` in the file routes).

content_type.description: Classified by the server from the name and bytes, never taken from the uploader.

view.description: How a chat should show it; `none` means download only.

origin.description: `agent`: published by the session. `user`: attached by a person.

version.description: 1 for the first file of this name and origin, then 2, 3, …

latest_version.description: The highest version of this name and origin.
Always this file's own version: the newest of its name.

previous.description: The version this one follows; null for the first of its name.

seq.description: Monotonic per session; the cursor for after_seq.

kind.description: The event type, e.g. assistant, tool_use, webhook. The set is open: treat a kind you do not know as data to skip. `start_stage` reports start progress; `capabilities` reports what the session has loaded (payload: CapabilitiesPayload) and only the latest one describes the session.

CapabilitiesPayload.description: Payload of a `capabilities` event: what the session's engine has loaded. Engine-neutral data; a group the engine does not report is absent, a reported group with nothing in it has `items: []`. Every string is display text (control and format characters removed, lengths capped); MCP server configuration is never included.

engine.description: Engine id: claude, native, codex, hermes, ...

version.description: The engine's own version, when it reports one.

cwd.description: Short display form of the working directory, never a full host path.

note.description: Where the report comes from, for display.

total.description: Item count before the per-group cap (500); absent when nothing was cut.

detail.description: e.g. a plugin version or an MCP server's tool count.

terminal.description: True for `ended` and `error`: the work is over.

last_assistant_message.description: Text of the most recent assistant event.

auto_stop.description: Whether this session was started one-shot: the runner ended it when its first turn was done.

token_endpoint.description: Filled in by core in the aggregate manifest.

ui.description: The UI this runner distributes for apps built on it. Absent when this build packed no package.

chat_package.description: The npm package that renders a session's chat over this contract. `npm i <url>` installs it; `sha512` is the tarball's integrity string for a lockfile; `docs_url` is its README.
